task_prompt:
The subject-manifest trust boundary rejects some manifests that are perfectly legal.

A manifest may legitimately reuse the SAME nested object in more than one place — for example a configuration that references one shared options object from two different sections. Today such a manifest is refused with a "cyclic value is not a JsonValue" error, even though it contains no cycle at all.

A manifest that genuinely contains a recursive back-edge (an object that contains itself, directly or indirectly) must still be refused.

Fix the validator so that only true recursive back-edges are refused. Do not change any test file.
task_prompt_solution_blindness: The prompt names the SYMPTOM (a legal manifest is refused with a 'cyclic value' error) and the required OUTCOME (only true recursive back-edges are refused). It does NOT name WeakSet, Set, recursion stacks, ancestors, try/finally, or any data structure.

ML06A-02: shared sibling OBJECTS are accepted
ML06A-03: shared sibling ARRAYS are accepted
ML06A-04: shared substructure at DIFFERENT DEPTHS is accepted
ML06A-05: a DIRECT cycle is rejected
ML06A-06: an INDIRECT cycle is rejected
ML06A-07: a cycle WITHIN shared substructure is rejected
ML06A-08: the existing invalid-value behaviour is preserved
ML06A-10: the input is not reshaped and the returned value is the SAME reference
